transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-05-29
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (CTO, NimbusCore), Laura Gomez (Head Infra), Evan Roberts (Security Eng), Anika Shah (ML Platform)

Summary (auto): Align on pilot guardrails — exchange security artifacts, plan load/latency bench, map SSO and RBAC, define success criteria.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Maya Chen: ok everyone thanks for carving out time, I know schedules are tight. quick round of intros?
[00:08] Samir Patel: Samir here, CTO at NimbusCore, we run the inference infra and platform for our products, excited to see how Redwood might slot in.
[00:15] Laura Gomez: Laura, infrastructure lead, we'll own networking and VPC parts.
[00:19] Evan Roberts: Evan, security — I'll own the SOC 2/ISO gating and log review.
[00:23] Anika Shah: Anika, ML Platform, will run the benchmarks with Diego.
[00:28] Maya Chen: great — Diego and Priya from our side, we'll cover the bench plan and SSO mapping.
[00:33] Diego Alvarez: hi all. quick agenda: security artifacts, SSO/RBAC mapping, deployment option for pilot, benchmark targets, next steps. sound right?
[00:40] Samir Patel: yep, that's it. primary ask from execs is: no data leaves our VPC during pilot, and we need traceable audit logs for every request.
[00:49] Maya Chen: noted. to be explicit — Redwood offers three modes: hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, or private VPC/on-prem. For this pilot are you leaning to private?
[00:58] Laura Gomez: private VPC probably, we need egress controls and to keep logs within our tenancy. but curious about the overhead — is there a lightweight dedicated option?
[01:07] Priya Rao: light dedicated is possible — reserved capacity in customer VPC with peered networking. we can also place the control plane in a customer-managed network in our Private offering. tradeoffs are around setup time and SLA.
[01:19] Evan Roberts: small aside — we require SOC2 Type II or ISO27001 evidence. do you have the certified docs?
[01:25] Maya Chen: yes, we can share a redacted SOC2 report and ISO 27001 certification extract. we'll also provide an audit log sample and KMS integration notes.
[01:32] Anika Shah: for benchmarks, we usually test with three model variants: a full fp16 model, a quantized int8-like variant, and a smaller specialized model. typical sequence lengths?
[01:41] Anika Shah: our mean is 120 tokens, tail at 512 for longer prompts.
[01:45] Diego Alvarez: great — for throughput we should know concurrency and expected qps: Samir, what are you targeting for pilot?
[01:52] Samir Patel: start with 50 concurrent users, roughly 250 requests per second, average response ~200 tokens. long term scale to 1k rps but pilot lower.
[02:01] Priya Rao: to map that to tokens/sec — 250 rps * 200 tokens = 50k tokens/sec, that's a meaningful load for a single node; we'll likely need batching + multiple replicas.
[02:10] Laura Gomez: okay, and latency SLO? execs want interaction feel near instant.
[02:15] Maya Chen: typical acceptance we suggest: 95th percentile generation latency under 250ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens), and tail under 1s for longer ones, but we'll tune per model.
[02:24] Samir Patel: our product team asked for 95p < 300ms for the majority of flows. can you commit to that in a pilot?
[02:30] Diego Alvarez: we can aim for that in dedicated/private with optimized kernels and proper batching; bench run will validate.
[02:36] Evan Roberts: back to security — audit logs: we need per-request metadata (request id, user id, model id, latency, token usage) and retention for 13 months, plus export to our logstore. can you stream or push logs to an S3-compatible endpoint or do you only offer control-plane access?
[02:50] Priya Rao: we support streaming audit logs to customer-owned sinks in Private deployments; for hosted we can provide log exports or delivery to customer S3 with encryption. retention and retention policies are configurable.
[03:00] Evan Roberts: encryption at rest — KMS/HSM options? we need customer-managed keys.
[03:04] Maya Chen: yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for private and dedicated; HSM integrations available for on-prem in some packages. we'll include the KMS integration note in the security pack.
[03:14] Samir Patel: SSO is next — we use Okta. need SAML-based SSO + SCIM for provisioning. also RBAC so product teams can't touch infra configs.
[03:24] Diego Alvarez: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM. we have an SSO mapping template: roles in Redwood map to your groups, and we can pre-populate role matrix.
[03:33] Anika Shah: what's the granularity of RBAC? can we limit who can create routes, who can see cost, and who can run benches?
[03:39] Priya Rao: yes, roles include Admin, Infra, Dev, ReadOnly, and we can add custom roles. actions are scoped per route/model.
[03:46] Laura Gomez: audit trail integrity is important. we want immutable logs and tamper evidence.
[03:50] Maya Chen: logs are append-only in the customer sink; we also support signed audit archives and can provide hashed manifests for integrity checks.
[03:59] Evan Roberts: any known gaps — like missing fields or issues that previous customers raised?
[04:03] Diego Alvarez: sometimes customers want more fine-grained session tracing — we can surface user-action traces but need to map your user ids in SAML/SCIM. also, model-level request redaction isn't automatic; we can apply tokenization or PII masking if needed.
closing_recap: Agreed: Redwood to send security pack and SSO/RBAC template. Customer will provide traces and sample payloads. Plan: schedule benchmark week of 2025-06-09, acceptance = functional pass + performance (95p latency targets) + security review. Follow-up meeting to confirm benchmark config.
notes_for_engineers: Benchmark target: validate ~50k tokens/sec with 250 rps average at pilot. Primary checks: 95p latency <300ms for common flows, audit log completeness (request id, user id, model id, tokens), KMS key rotation test, SAML SCIM provisioning and RBAC enforcement. Bring preconfigured load scripts and model quantization profiles.
